question.value: Is the massive DRG overdensity CL J1001 at z~2.5 a collapsed, cluster-sized halo, and what are the star formation and quiescent properties of its members?

evidence.quote: We report the discovery of a remarkable concentration of massive galaxies with extended X-ray emission at $z_{spec} = 2.506$
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00539.S.
observed as a candidate of lensed sources with ALMA at band-7 (870 $\mu$m)
we detected three sources in CO(5-4) down to integrated line fluxes of $\sim$0.6 Jy km s$^{-1}$ (5$\sigma$)
Seven of them are at $2.494 \leq z_{spec} \leq 2.512$, which are consistent with being cluster members.
Eleven galaxies were detected in CO(1-0) down to integrated line fluxes 0.05 Jy km s$^{-1}$
We combined the latest Chandra and $XMM-Newton$ surveys of the COSMOS field

evidence.quote: we fit the 250 $\mu$m to 1.1mm data points with an FIR SED consisting of a coupled single-dust-temperature blackbody and mid-infrared power law described in (cite: Casey:2012a)
A (cite: Salpeter:1955) initial mass function (IMF) is adopted to derive stellar masses and SFRs.
